observed_result: The receptor-driven gate and eligibility window run, and the gate, decay, delayed-feedback and close-off effects pass separately. (1) Gate closed (TestReceptorGateClosedWhenConcentrationIsZero): a timeline that never releases leaves occupancy 0, plastic stays exactly 0 while the forward output is bit for bit the chemistry-only run, eligibility still tracks the activity to 0.4579164488274385 (non-zero), and the report carries GateFromReceptor true, WindowFromReceptor false, Steps 3. (2) Gate opens with occupancy (TestReceptorGateOpensWithOccupancy): the row-1 occupancy is chemOcc1 = 0.611481100422978; mid eligibility 0.2151700772189281 and mid plastic 0.1315724355959273, which equals occ1 * elig1 = 0.611481100422978 * 0.2151700772189281 exactly; the final fast state rises above the closed-gate run to eligibility 0.4903410193303885 and plastic 0.3052627141695012. (3) Window changes decay_e (TestReceptorWindowChangesDecayE): window(occ1) = 0.5 - 0.4*0.611481100422978 = 0.2554075598308088 (clamped into [0.1, 0.9]); the final eligibility 0.4158818857906775 is below 0.4579164488274385, what a constant 0.5 decay would leave, so a delayed-feedback trace under a shorter window is distinguishable from the constant one; plastic stays 0 because no gate is declared. (4) The distinction tests reject the wrong combinations: TestRuleReceptorFieldsValidated refuses gate_scale without gate_receptor, negative gate_receptor, decay_e_min 0, decay_e_max 1, decay_e_base out of [min, max], and decay_e_span without decay_e_receptor; TestStepWithDecayEOverride hand-computes the per-step DecayE override (eligibility = decay_e*elig + pre*post: 0.5*0+1*1 = 1, then 0.25*1+1 = 1.25, then 0.75*1.25+1 = 1.9375) and refuses DecayE of 1.0 or NaN; TestWindowAndGateFor clamps WindowFor to DecayEMin/DecayEMax (occupancy 0 -> 0.5, 1 -> 0.8, -1 -> 0.3, NaN -> 0.5) and returns GateFor(0.25) = 2*0.25 = 0.5, and returns false on both without a declared receptor. (5) On the individual: TestReceptorRuleRejectedWithoutChemistry refuses a receptor-named rule when no chemistry serves it (and a receptor index 7 out of range) but accepts chemistry-first then the rule and rule-first then chemistry; TestExplicitGateCannotCombineWithReceptorGate refuses a nonzero explicit gate on a receptor-gated rule with an error mentioning both "cannot be combined" and "receptor" and commits nothing (plastic 0, eligibility 0); TestDisableChemistryRefusedWhileRuleNeedsReceptor keeps the chemistry layer on until the receptor-referencing rule is gone, on both the gate and the window path.
assumption_statement: Gate and window values come from the mean occupancy of the named receptor on the current row; occupancy is produced by the ticket 21 chemistry layer (ticket 21 rules and evidence in evidence/MOD-02/, MOD-03/, MOD-04/), and this ticket adds no concentration or occupancy computation of its own. Delayed-feedback and decay basics are established in the ticket 18 LRN-05 evidence; this stage only proves the window changes the eligibility trace as occupancy rises and that the gate opens with occupancy. The gate and window fixtures are hypothesis-only engineering declarations (one hypothesized receptor, engineering Kd and N); no biological claim is made about which cell carries which receptor. A rule may be gated either by the receptor or by a caller-supplied gate sequence, never both; the receptor is read from the chemistry layer, so the layer cannot be disabled while a rule names a receptor.
limitations: Fixture scale only: two isolated neurons, one edge, one hypothesized receptor, three rows. No whole-brain, real-data, cross-platform or performance run.
Only hebbian_rate is verified with a receptor gate on an individual; the stdp_pair path shares the same plasticity.Model machinery but no receptor-gate individual test runs it here.
The window is verified with one receptor only; a rule declaring two receptors (one for the gate and one for the window) has no coverage in this log.
The closed-form constants are the fixture's own hand tables (PLASTIC decay_c/decay_p halving rules of the chemistry fixture, reported literals), not a measurement or a biological parameter.
